title: Oop and the 'sandwich'
body: In Scene 2 of the play, Think-Tank decides that the books in the Centerville Public Library are sandwiches, 'the main staple of Earth diet', and orders Captain Omega to eat one to confirm his opinion. Omega passes the order to Lieutenant Iota, saying that poor Iota has not had her breakfast. Iota, in turn, says it would be impolite to eat before her Sergeant and orders Sergeant Oop to eat the sandwich immediately. With Omega and Iota saluting him 'for the glory of Mars', Oop bites a corner of the book, chewing and swallowing while making terrible faces, and then coughs while the others pound him on the back. Think-Tank asks, 'Was it not delicious, Sergeant Oop?' Oop salutes and replies, 'That is correct, sir. It was not delicious.' He adds that he does not know how Earthlings get such sandwiches down without water, since they are 'dry as Martian dust'.

title: Think-Tank hears the rhymes
body: After taking their vitamins, the Martian crew 'decipher' the code in a large, colourful copy of Mother Goose. Omega reads: 'Mistress Mary, quite contrary, / How does your garden grow? / With cockle shells and silver bells / And pretty maids all in a row.' Oop laughs at the idea of pretty maids growing in a garden, but Think-Tank is alarmed. He declares that the Earthlings have learnt to combine agriculture and mining, growing crops of rare metals such as silver, and even high explosives, and he tells the invasion fleet to hold. Iota then reads 'Hey diddle diddle', in which the cow jumps over the moon and the dish runs away with the spoon. Think-Tank orders the crew to cease laughing and says the Earthlings have taught their domesticated animals musical culture and space techniques, adding that even their dogs have a sense of humour and that Earth may be launching an interplanetary attack of millions of cows.
